Asian stocks plunge: Kospi tumbles over 7%, Nikkei sheds 3,000 points as AI-linked shares drag markets
sum: Asian stocks suffered brutal sell-offs on Friday, with Taiwan and South Korea taking the biggest hits as investors turned cautious amid AI fears. The plunge came as Wall Street witnessed its worst session in 18 months, wiping out $2.5 trillion in investor wealth in one of the biggest single-day losses.
Asian stock markets witnessed a broad-based sell-off on Friday, with Taiwan and South Korea bearing the brunt of the losses as the rout in technology stocks spread across the region.

The sell-off saw Taiwan's weighted index plunge 8%, while South Korea's KOSPI dropped more than 7%. Japan's Nikkei 225 also declined over 3,000 points or 5.95%. The losses extended to Singapore, where the Straits Times index fell 2.20% to 5,180. Hong Kong's Hang Seng index was also trading lower during early trading.

Technology stocks were among the worst hit, with semiconductor companies facing particularly heavy selling. South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix plunged more than 8%, while Samsung Electronics shed 7%. LG Innotek and LG Display also fell 10% and 7.7%, respectively, as investors dumped technology shares across the country.

Japanese technology stocks were not spared either. Semiconductor-related companies witnessed sharp declines, with chip-testing equipment maker Advantest plunging 12.2% and Tokyo Electron sliding 7.3%.
Memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings fell nearly 10%, while Renesas Electronics declined 7.5%.

Taiwan's semiconductor sector also came under intense pressure. Contract chipmaker TSMC slumped 9.6%, while electronics manufacturers Hon Hai Precision Industry, also known as Foxconn, and Foxconn Technology dropped 9.4% and 9.1%, respectively.

U.S. Midterm Elections Shift Balance of Power; Taiwan Stock Market Plunges Over 500 Points in Early Trading, 43,000-Point Line Breached
sum: Democrats won the U.S. midterm elections, dispelling the political uncertainty that Wall Street had previously borne, but markets quickly shifted to worrying that Democratic control of Congress would create more resistance and restrictions for data center construction. Of the four major U.S. stock indices, only the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index closed lower on Wednesday (Nov. 4). That wait-and-see atmosphere carried over to the Taiwan stock market, where the weighted index opened Thursday (Nov. 5) at 42,666.13 points, down 282.78 points. Selling pressure continued to emerge in early trading, with the index at one point plunging 517.94 points to a low of 42,430.97, breaching the 43,000-point round-number threshold once again.

Heavyweight stocks were the main drag on the broader market. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (2330) opened down NT$10 at NT$2,250; MediaTek (2454) opened sharply lower by NT$115 at NT$3,600; Hon Hai (2317) slipped NT$1 to NT$239. In the previous trading session, the Taiwan stock market had already opened higher and closed lower after the election results were settled, finishing down 358.63 points, or 0.83%, at 42,948.91. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing closed that day at NT$2,260, down NT$35, indicating that market concerns about the post-election policy direction had not dissipated with the announcement of the results.

Looking back at Wednesday's session, the Taiwan stock market opened up 322.88 points at 43,630.42, but buying momentum subsequently faded and the index turned from gains to losses, declining steadily. Heavyweight stocks showed mixed performance: Hon Hai closed at NT$240, down NT$5.5; MediaTek closed at NT$3,715, bucking the trend with a gain of NT$40; United Microelectronics (2303) closed at NT$105.5, up NT$2.5; Delta Electronics (2308) closed at NT$1,220, down NT$50. Financial stocks were similarly mixed: Fubon Financial Holding (2881) closed at NT$154.5, up NT$0.5; Cathay Financial Holding (2882) closed at NT$111, down NT$2; CTBC Financial Holding (2891) closed at NT$73.2, down NT$1; Mega Financial Holding (2886) closed at NT$53.5, up NT$0.3.
Note: Nov. 5 data reflects early trading performance, not final closing figures.

Taiwan Stocks Plunge 1,612 Points in a Single Day; Guo Zherong Cites Nomura Report: Negative Cash Flow Misread, Not a Bearish Signal
sum: Taiwan's Weighted Index opened lower and fell further on the 3rd, touching an intraday low of 43,191.58 before closing down 1,612.60 points, or 3.59%, at 43,307.54 — decisively breaking below the 44,000-point threshold — with single-day turnover of NT$928.058 billion (approximately $28.3 billion). Measured over the past month, the benchmark has now tumbled roughly 6,000 points, and concerns over whether a bear market has officially arrived are heating up rapidly. Moore Investment Advisory Chief Investment Officer Guo Zherong stepped forward at this juncture, citing the latest Nomura Securities report to argue that the selloff stems from excessive market sentiment rather than a deterioration in corporate fundamentals. He stressed that "the market will eventually give fundamentals their due."

Guo Zherong analyzed that the market has been continuously magnifying political uncertainty ahead of the U.S. election as well as the disruption to oil prices and market sentiment from shifting U.S.-Iran tensions. These headline factors have become reasons for investors to sell holdings, but they should not be equated directly with a deteriorating corporate profit outlook. He believes that once panic gradually subsides, capital will ultimately re-examine corporate earnings and industry trends, giving the market a chance to return to fundamentals. He therefore maintained his medium- to long-term view that the Taiwan Weighted Index will challenge 50,000 by year-end and reach 100,000 over the next three years.

The Nomura Securities report cited by Guo Zherong centers on clarifying a misunderstanding about the AI industry. The report notes that investors have directly interpreted cloud giants' "negative free cash flow" as "AI is unprofitable and earnings are declining," when in fact they are conflating two concepts: profit and cash flow. Cloud providers are currently in the early stage of heavy investment in AI infrastructure, aggressively purchasing GPUs and developing their own TPU chips; it is the massive capital expenditure that has temporarily turned cash flow negative. Yet the three major cloud providers posted year-on-year revenue growth of 56% over the same period, showing that real demand for AI computing power remains strong.

Taiwan's Delta Electronics Stock Halves From Peak; Market Cap Overtaken by Hon Hai, Slips to No. 4
sum: The Taiwan stock market fell sharply intraday on November 3, and shares of AI power supply leader Delta Electronics (2308.TW) hit new lows in tandem, ending the session down NT$85, or 6.27%, at NT$1,270 — an eight-month low. Compared with the intraday peak of NT$2,585 set in late May, the stock has effectively halved. Market capitalization rankings were reshuffled accordingly, with Delta overtaken by Hon Hai (2317.TW) and knocked out of the top three listed companies to fourth place.

According to Taiwan Stock Exchange market capitalization statistics for listed companies, Delta's latest market value is NT$3.2988 trillion (approximately $100.6 billion), while Hon Hai climbed to third place at NT$3.4555 trillion (approximately $105.4 billion). Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (2330.TW) remains the market cap leader at NT$59.5147 trillion (approximately $1.8 trillion), with MediaTek (2454.TW) second at NT$5.8981 trillion (approximately $179.9 billion); ASE Technology Holding (3711.TW) ranks fifth at NT$3.0131 trillion (approximately $91.9 billion). The top five market cap companies are all electronics heavyweights.

In fact, the two companies' market values had already crossed at the November 2 close. That day, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing's market value was about NT$60.4224 trillion (approximately $1.8 trillion) and MediaTek's about NT$6.3717 trillion (approximately $194.3 billion), with Hon Hai at NT$3.533 trillion (approximately $107.7 billion) taking third place and Delta close behind at NT$3.5197 trillion (approximately $107.3 billion) — a gap of only about NT$13.3 billion (approximately $405.6 million). Delta touched its limit-down price of NT$1,335 intraday on October 30; although it rebounded NT$20 to close at NT$1,355 on November 2, Hon Hai rose 2.24% the same day, and Delta failed to hold its ranking. The stock weakened further on November 3; based on the intraday low of NT$1,310, its market value was about NT$3.4 trillion (approximately $103.7 billion), evaporating roughly another NT$116.9 billion (approximately $3.6 billion) from the prior trading day.

Taiwan shares end down but off lows amid U.S. volatility
sum: Taipei, Nov. 2 (CNA) Shares in Taiwan closed down Monday but recovered from the day's low as the market remained concerned about volatility in the United States amid questions over massive spending on AI infrastructure, dealers said.

The Taiex, the Taiwan Stock Exchange's benchmark index, ended down 291.69 points, or 0.65 percent, at 44,920.14 after moving between 44,399.10 and 45,156.17. Turnover totaled NT$758.88 billion (US$23.25 billion) following Friday's NT$939.61 billion.

The index faced heavy pressure in the early-morning session, tumbling 812.73 points to the day's low, largely on a 2.86 percent fall on the tech-heavy Nasdaq index and a 7.20 percent plunge on the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index Friday, dealers said.

However, the local market recouped most of its earlier losses as bargain hunters picked up shares in select market laggards, including smartphone IC designer MediaTek and iPhone assembler and AI server maker Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., dealers added.
"For bargain hunters, this morning's losses created buying opportunities for some market laggards with MediaTek and Hon Hai included," Hua Nan Securities analyst Kevin Su said.
MediaTek rose 1.40 percent to close at NT$3,970.00, off a low of NT$3,795.00 and Hon Hai gained 2.24 percent to end at NT$251.00, off a low of NT$242.50.
Also a focus of bargain hunting, power management solutions provider Delta Electronics Inc. added 1.50 percent to close at NT$1,355.00.

Hon Hai stock: October revenue is due on November 5
sum: Hon Hai is due to report its October revenue on Thursday, November 5, giving investors the next scheduled read on demand for AI servers and other electronics. The figure will arrive one week before the company's third-quarter results, according to TickerGrove.

Foxconn's third-quarter revenue reached 3.03 trillion Taiwan dollars, up 47.12 percent from a year earlier and 20.44 percent from the second quarter. The company said cloud and networking products led the quarter, reflecting demand for AI-related shipments.

September revenue was 1.16 trillion Taiwan dollars, the first month above that threshold, while the company's four segments grew year over year in the quarter. The September monthly revenue announcement was published by Hon Hai Technology Group on October 5.

The November 5 release will cover sales rather than profit or margins. The November 12 quarterly report will therefore remain the more complete test of whether stronger AI-related shipments translated into earnings. Foxconn has said fourth-quarter AI activity should continue to grow alongside the traditional second-half peak season, while warning that political and economic conditions remain volatile.

MLCC Price-Hike Theme Ignites Passive Component Limit-Up Wave; Taiwan Stock Market Surges 693 Points to Reclaim 46,000
sum: Taiwan's stock market staged a powerful rebound on September 4, with the TAIEX surging 693.47 points to close at 46,551.13, a gain of 1.51%, reclaiming the 46,000-point level. The passive components sector ignited across the board on MLCC price-hike momentum, with Yageo, Walsin Technology, Taiwan Chinsan Electronic Industrial, and three other stocks hitting daily limit-up simultaneously, making the group the strongest bullish indicator on the board. All three major institutional investor categories turned net buyers with combined purchases of NT$62.872 billion (approximately $2.0 billion), ending a two-session selling streak.

U.S. stocks closed broadly higher in the previous session as bond yields retreated and large-cap tech stocks strengthened, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average surging 624.16 points and the Nasdaq rising 1.4%, injecting a shot of confidence into Taiwan's bulls. The TAIEX opened higher at 45,991 points, briefly surged to 46,603 points in early trading — up as much as 745 points — before gains moderated slightly, closing at 46,551.13 with turnover of NT$825.626 billion (approximately $26.1 billion). Across the main board and the TPEx combined, 1,371 stocks advanced versus 465 decliners, with 36 stocks limit-up and 5 limit-down, signaling a clear resurgence in bullish momentum.
Passive Components Explode Across the Board; Six Stocks Limit-Up Lead the Charge

The passive components sector was the biggest highlight of the session. According to TrendForce's latest MLCC industry research, South Korean giant SEMCO recently took the lead in raising Q4 2026 quotes for OEM and ODM customers, departing from its past practice of only adjusting prices for distributors. Market participants interpreted this as a sign that the MLCC price-hike wave is expanding from the channel level to end customers, making the industry's upward pricing signal even more definitive.

Buoyed by this catalyst, Yageo (2327.TW) closed limit-up at NT$562, up NT$51 or 9.98%, with trading volume expanding notably. Walsin Technology (2492.TW), Taiwan Chinsan Electronic Industrial (8042.TW), Holy Stone Enterprise (3026.TW), Viking Tech (3624.TW), and TA-I Technology (2478.TW) also hit limit-up simultaneously.

sum: - Elon Musk said SpaceX will build its AI infrastructure exclusively on Nvidia chips going forward.
- Nvidia's manufacturing partner, Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., reported a 54.2% increase in July sales, signaling sustained demand for global AI infrastructure buildout.
- Retail sentiment for NVDA shifted to 'bullish' from 'neutral', amid 'high' message volume.

Nvidia Corp.'s stock rose nearly 2% in early premarket trading on Wednesday, bucking a selloff in the broader market and chipmakers, after SpaceX picked the chipmaker as its exclusive supplier of AI chips.
CEO Elon Musk said SpaceX will build its AI infrastructure exclusively on Nvidia chips going forward.

"Going forward, we've decided to build exclusively on Nvidia, because we think the Vera Rubin architecture is the best architecture. We think it's the best AI computer, and we greatly value our close cooperation and partnership on many levels with Nvidia. We're exclusive to Nvidia," Musk said in SpaceX's analyst call.
If NVDA's move holds in Wednesday's regular session, it would be the fifth straight day of gains for the stock. Shares of AMD, SpaceX's current chip supplier, fell 8% in premarket.

Taiwan shares ended flat after a big swing
sum: Taipei, Aug. 4 (CNA) Shares in Taiwan closed little changed after a big swing of more than 1,000 points Tuesday as selling emerged to erode initial gains with investors shrugging off a rally in the United States overnight, dealers said.

The Taiex, the Taiwan Stock Exchange's benchmark index, ended down 25.75 points, or 0.06 percent, at 43,360.66 after moving between 42,895.81 and 43,912.77. Turnover totaled NT$1.036 trillion (US$34.5 billion).

Despite a 2.13 percent increase on the tech-heavy Nasdaq index overnight, "the Taiex still failed to sustain its earlier upturn as large-cap semiconductor stocks, in particular TSMC (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.), traded in negative territory," Concord Securities analyst Kerry Huang said.

"TSMC remained in consolidation so the entire main board just followed," Huang said. "Judging from today's movement, I suspect the Taiex faced stiff technical resistance around the 20-day moving average of 43,785 points."
Contract chipmaker TSMC, which accounts for over 40 percent of total market value, closed down 2.11 percent at NT$2,320.00 and its losses led the semiconductor subindex to fall by 1.37 percent.
Smartphone IC designer MediaTek Inc. lost 1.15 percent to end at NT$3,865.00, and IC packaging and testing firm ASE Technology Holding Co. shed 4.10 percent to close at NT$585.00.

Bucking the downturn, shares in memory chip suppliers Nanya Technology Corp. and Winbond Electronics Corp. soared 10 percent, the maximum daily increase, to end at NT$436.00 and NT$157.00, respectively, on a global supply shortage.

items.t: Hang Seng Index Rises for Fourth Day, Up 0.41%; AI Stocks Diverge as Foxconn Reportedly Lands $52 Billion SpaceX Order
sum: Despite heavy losses in overseas chip stocks that stirred market anxiety, Hong Kong equities demonstrated resilience on Monday, lifted by Chinese internet giants and the auto sector. The Hang Seng Index rose 0.41% to close higher for a fourth straight session, while the Hang Seng Tech Index outperformed with a 0.61% gain.

Large-cap Chinese tech stocks served as the market's anchor. Heavyweights including Tencent Holdings (00700.HK), Alibaba (09988.HK), Meituan (03690.HK), JD.com (09618.HK), and NetEase (09999.HK) all advanced, effectively offsetting downward pressure from the semiconductor sector. Xiaomi (01810.HK) extended its recent strong run, providing a particularly notable boost to the Hang Seng Tech Index.

The session opened on a positive note, with all three major indices gapping higher. The Hang Seng Index opened up 0.26%, the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index gained 0.38%, and the Hang Seng Tech Index rose 0.64%. Beyond the broad-based strength in internet names, power utilities, automakers, online healthcare platforms, and beer stocks also advanced, signaling that risk appetite had not been entirely extinguished by external headwinds.

A blockbuster order report ignited market sentiment at the single-stock level. According to market sources, Taiwan-based Hon Hai Precision Industry (2317.TW), better known as Foxconn, has reportedly secured an AI server order from SpaceX valued at up to $52 billion. The news sent shares of Foxconn subsidiary FIH Mobile (02038.HK) soaring as much as 9.56% intraday, making it one of the most closely watched names in the Hong Kong market.

Beneath the surface, however, the semiconductor and AI-related sectors exhibited stark structural divergence. Dragged down by an overnight slump in US chip stocks and early-session weakness in Japanese and South Korean equity markets, Hong Kong-listed semiconductor and hardware names came under heavy selling pressure. Industry leaders SMIC (00981.HK) and Hua Hong Semiconductor (01347.HK) briefly rallied in early trading before quickly reversing course, failing to participate in the broader market's stabilization. Memory chip stocks, PCB-related names, and optical communications plays were among the hardest hit.

Taiwan shares edge lower as tech stocks rebound, financials gain
sum: Taipei, July 27 (CNA) Shares in Taiwan ended slightly lower Monday, as large-cap tech stocks rebounded from early losses, while rotational buying in the financial sector helped limit losses, dealers said.

The Taiex, the Taiwan Stock Exchange's benchmark index, ended down 20.65 points, or 0.05 percent, at 43,634.19 after moving between 42,969.48 and 43,868.15. Turnover totaled NT$717.69 billion (US$22.18 billion).
Concord Securities analyst Kerry Huang said the index's initial losses reflected concerns that massive AI investments could fail to generate adequate revenue for major cloud service providers.

"After Alphabet (Google's parent company) reported last week that its free cash flows had turned negative, investors have remained cautious about other companies in the sector, which will release their results this week," Huang said, referring to Microsoft and Meta, which will hold investor conferences Thursday U.S. time and Amazon, whose investor conference is scheduled for Friday.
"Fortunately, large-cap semiconductor stocks bounced back from their earlier losses, particularly memory chip suppliers, helping the electronics sector and the broader market," Huang said.
Among the major memory chip suppliers, Nanya Technology Corp. rose 8.73 percent to close at NT$436.00, and Winbond Electronics Corp. gained 3.56 percent to end at NT$160.00.

Also in the semiconductor industry, contract chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), which accounts for more than 40 percent of the local market's total value, closed unchanged at NT$2,350.00 after rising from a low of NT$2,330.00. Smartphone IC designer MediaTek Inc. lost 1.87 percent to close at NT$3,680.00 after rebounding from a low of NT$3,525.00.

items.t: Taiwan Stocks Surge 1,783 Points in Record Rally; Yageo, UMC, MediaTek Emerge as New Bull Market Leaders
sum: Taiwan's stock market staged a dramatic and forceful rebound on July 21, just one trading session after Friday's nearly 3,000-point crash that rewrote the record books for the largest single-day point decline. The Taiwan Weighted Index soared 1,783.17 points, a surge of 4.2%, to close at 44,232.87, setting a new all-time record for the largest single-day closing point gain and successfully reclaiming both the 5-day moving average and the quarterly line. While trading value contracted to NT$835.62 billion (approximately $25.8 billion) from the previous session's near-trillion-dollar volume, capital flows clearly pivoted from panic selling toward aggressive buying of major electronic heavyweight stocks. Notably, this rebound was no longer a one-man show driven solely by TSMC (2330). Heavyweight names including Yageo (2327), UMC (2303), and MediaTek (2454) simultaneously strengthened, emerging as new standard-bearers for the bulls.
Heavyweight Stocks Rally Broadly; TSMC Leads but No Longer Dominates Alone

Taiwan's "sacred mountain protecting the nation," TSMC, continued to serve as the vanguard for the bulls on July 21, surging NT$90, or 3.88%, to close at NT$2,410. Its trading value reached NT$71.3 billion (approximately $2.2 billion), firmly securing the top spot in market turnover. Foreign investors modestly bought back 4,976 shares on the day, signaling that market confidence is warming alongside the stock's rebound. Earlier, during the market turmoil on July 20, TSMC had bucked the trend by rising NT$30 to close at NT$2,320, with trading value hitting NT$105.15 billion (approximately $3.2 billion), offering an early signal of stabilization.

Following TSMC's second-quarter earnings release and an upward revision to its full-year outlook, Morgan Stanley believes AI demand will continue to drive utilization rates for advanced processes and advanced packaging capacity. The firm maintained its "Overweight" rating on TSMC and raised its target price from NT$2,888 to NT$2,988. TSMC CFO Wendell Huang, in an exclusive interview with CNBC, also disclosed that the company's additional US$100 billion investment in Arizona is a response to strong demand from U.S. customers, as it actively expands advanced process capacity.

SPCX Stock Rises Overnight Even As Elon Musk Shoots Down Report Of $52B Foxconn-Nvidia Order As 'Fake News'
sum: - Musk called the report of 13,000 Nvidia GB300 server racks “fake news.”
- The reported $52 billion value was based on an estimated $4 million cost per rack.
- The company is also expanding cloud capacity through arrangements involving Google and Anthropic.

SpaceX (SPCX) shares rose 1% overnight heading into Monday after CEO Elon Musk dismissed a report claiming that the rocket and satellite company had placed a $52 billion order with Foxconn for Nvidia-powered AI servers.
SPCX stock fell 5% on Friday, extending its weekly decline to 15%.

“This is fake news,” Musk said on X in response to a post summarizing the reported agreement. Taiwan’s Economic Daily said that Hon Hai Precision Industry, better known as Foxconn, had secured its first contract to manufacture AI servers for SpaceX. According to the report, SpaceX was preparing to deploy more than 13,000 server racks built around Nvidia’s GB300 platform. The estimated $52 billion value was based on an assumed cost of $4 million per rack rather than a disclosed contract price.

Citrini analyst Jukan said on X that Foxconn had displaced the dominance of Dell Technologies and Super Micro Computer in supplying AI server infrastructure to SpaceX. It also claimed deliveries would begin in late 2026 and continue into the first quarter of 2027. Chairman Young Liu has previously said Foxconn expects to capture more than 40% of the global AI server market, while shipments of advanced AI racks are projected to increase through the end of the year.

Taiwan Stocks Plunge Over 2,000 Points Intraday, Breaching 44,000; UMC, Yageo, Nan Ya Hit Limit Down; High-Priced Shares Lose NT$1,000 Threshold
sum: Taiwan's stock market encountered intense selling pressure today, with the intraday index plummeting more than 2,000 points at one stage, not only breaching the 44,000-point level but also directly testing support at the quarterly moving average. Hit by a double whammy of a heavy sell-off in U.S. technology stocks and a share price correction for TSMC following its earnings call, panic swept through the market. Over 1,500 stocks across the listed and over-the-counter boards fell, with multiple heavyweight and high-priced stocks tumbling, while UMC, Yageo, and Nan Ya Plastics hit their daily limit down.

All four major U.S. stock indices closed in the red on Thursday, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plummeting 4.29%, becoming the key factor that crushed Taiwan's market. Doubts arose over whether the massive capital expenditure on artificial intelligence (AI) can generate corresponding returns, and escalating geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East triggered heavy selling pressure on chip stocks. TSMC's ADR fell 2.32%, while UMC's ADR crashed 10.55%, causing Taiwan stock index futures to plunge nearly a thousand points in after-hours trading, setting the stage for today's collapse.

The TAIEX opened lower at 45,234.08 points today, quickly breaking below the 5-day moving average in early trading, with the decline steadily widening. As of 10:40 a.m., the TAIEX had plummeted 2,049.85 points to 43,575.13, a steep drop of 4.49%, with trading volume exploding to approximately NT$637.3 billion. The electronics sub-index tumbled 4.48%, while financial stocks were relatively resilient, slipping only 0.45%. The over-the-counter index, representing small and medium-sized stocks, plunged more than 5%, indicating a broad-based market rout.

Among heavyweight stocks, TSMC (2330), fresh from its earnings call, became a target for short sellers, dropping NT$100 intraday to NT$2,370, a decline of over 4%, significantly shrinking its market capitalization. MediaTek (2454) and Delta Electronics (2308) both fell more than 5%, while Hon Hai (2317) dropped over 2%. Notably, UMC (2303), Yageo (2327), and Nan Ya Plastics (1303) were directly locked at their daily limit down during the session under extremely heavy selling pressure.

items.t: Taiwan shares end sharply up as TSMC closes at day's high
sum: Taipei, July 1 (CNA) Shares in Taiwan closed sharply higher Wednesday, extending gains from the previous session, as contract chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) finished at the day's high after its American depositary receipts (ADRs) posted strong gains overnight, dealers said.

Following a 2.50 point increase Tuesday, the Taiex, the Taiwan Stock Exchange's benchmark index, ended up 893.08 points, or 1.94 percent, at 47,018.99 after moving between 46,234.70 and 47,293.10. Turnover totaled NT$1.302 trillion (US$40.85 billion).

"The Taiex was driven higher by the tech sector as buying focused on TSMC after U.S. chip stocks posted strong gains amid AI optimism worldwide," Cathay Futures Consultant analyst Tsai Ming-han said, referring to a 3.21 percent increase on the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index overnight.

After its ADRs rose 4.94 Tuesday, TSMC, which accounts for over 40 percent of total market value, rose 3.94 percent to close at NT$2,505.00. Its gains contributed about 760 points to the Taiex rise and sent the electronics index 2.44 percent higher.

"Judging from the buying, I think many investors were betting TSMC will give positive leads at its investor conference (slated for July 16)," Tsai said. "The stock could challenge its historical intraday high of NT$2,535 (on June 23) soon."

Buying spread to other semiconductor heavyweights with IC packaging and testing firm ASE Technology Holding Co. up 3.38 percent to end at NT$703.00 and smartphone IC designer MediaTek Inc. up 2.12 percent to close at NT$4,335.00.
However, memory chip supplier Nanya Technology Corp., lost 6.96 percent to end at NT$421.00.

items.t: Foxconn acquires 351.73 million shares in India arm investing USD 37.2 million
sum: Taiwanese electronics manufacturer Foxconn Singapore Pte Ltd has acquired around 351.73 million additional shares in its Indian arm Foxconn Hon Hai Technology India Mega Development Private Limited, as per an exchange filing.
- Foxconn invests USD 37.2 million in Indian arm with new share acquisition.
- Company holds 99.99999996% stake in its India subsidiary post-transaction.
- Investment reflects long-term strategy and no external purchase involved.

Taiwanese electronics manufacturer Foxconn Singapore has acquired around 351.73 million additional shares in its Indian arm Foxconn Hon Hai Technology India Mega Development Private Limited, as per an exchange filing.
As the board of directors approved the transaction on June 25, Wednesday, the company acquired the shares at INR 10 per share, amounting to a total investment of USD 37.2 million.
Following the transaction, Foxconn Singapore Pte Ltd. holds 23.18 billion shares in the India unit, accounting for a 99.99999996 per cent stake with a cumulative value of USD 2.82 billion.
